sdBackup.title: SD-card safety copy
sdBackup.hint: This is not how you back up your layout — use "Backup & share" → Export above for that. FlexibleLayouts automatically saves a copy of your whole layout to the printer's SD card every time you press Done, purely so a DWC settings reset (or switching between DWC 3.6 and 3.7) doesn't wipe it. Only use Restore if that's actually happened.

sdBackup.restoreNowHelp: Only for recovering after a DWC settings reset or a switch between DWC 3.6 and 3.7 wiped your layout — restores the automatic SD-card safety copy. For normal backup/sharing, use Export instead.

access.operatorHelp: Can run the machine (jog, home, run jobs/macros) but can't edit the layout, manage files, or leave this layout.

access.recoveryHint: Forgotten the Admin password? This is a soft, client-side deterrent, not real security — clear this plugin's settings (browser dev tools, or DWC's own plugin-data reset) to start over.
access.lockedHint: Access settings are locked — log in as Admin to view or change them.

configBackup.openHelp: Backup and restore the whole machine configuration (sys, macros, filaments) to your PC or the cloud.

create.redactHelpOn: Secrets are replaced with placeholders. A restore will ask you to supply or skip them.
create.objectModelHelp: The object model dump is always privacy-scrubbed (network identity, board serials) regardless of this switch - it's diagnostic context, never restored to a machine.
create.gatedNote: Creating a backup requires the Admin access level.
create.noScopeSelected: Select at least one thing to back up.

create.publicRepoBlockedBody: Pushing an unredacted backup to a public GitHub repository publishes your WiFi password and machine password to a permanently-archived, search-indexed location - rewriting history afterwards does not reliably undo this. Type CONFIRM to proceed anyway, or use a private repository, or turn on redaction.

restore.sourceDrop: or drop a backup ZIP here
restore.invalidArchive: This doesn't look like a Flexible Layouts config backup.
restore.repairHeading: Some restored files still contain redacted values
restore.repairIntro: These need to be resolved before the file can be restored - a redacted value would either fail on the machine or set it to the literal placeholder text.
restore.repairBulkKeepLive: Use current machine's values for all
restore.repairAmbiguous: Multiple different values found on the live machine - choose one:

restore.modeMergeHelp: Uploads every selected file, overwriting existing ones. Files on the machine that aren't in the backup are left alone.
restore.modeMirrorHelp: Also deletes files under a fully-selected directory that this backup doesn't contain. Never touches firmware files, directories the backup didn't cover, or Flexible Layouts' own SD backup.
restore.modeMirrorDisabledDifferentMachine: Mirror mode is disabled: this backup was taken on a different machine. Restoring files here (Merge) is safe; deleting files on this machine based on another machine's backup is not.
restore.modeMirrorPartialNote: {dir} is only partially selected, so it will be merged, not mirrored.

github.heading: GitHub
github.tokenHelp: A fine-grained token with Contents: Read and write on one repository. Never sent anywhere except api.github.com.
github.repoNotFound: Repository not found, or the token doesn't have access to it.
github.restoreNote: The Restore tab browses this machine's backup history (every past commit) and can restore any of them - or a different machine's, with a warning if it's not this one.
github.machineNameHelp: Overrides the folder name used for this machine's backups in the repo. Leave blank to use the machine's own name. Only affects new backups.

drive.heading: Google Drive
drive.unavailableBody: Google requires the page to be loaded over HTTPS (or localhost) to sign in, and this DuetWebControl is loaded over plain HTTP. This isn't something Flexible Layouts can work around. Use an HTTPS reverse proxy in front of your Duet, or download the backup locally and upload it to Drive yourself.
drive.clientIdHelp: Create your own in the Google Cloud console (Drive API enabled, Web application, this exact origin authorised). See the docs for step-by-step instructions.

dropbox.tokenHelp: Generate a long-lived token in the Dropbox App Console (App Console → your app → "Generated access token"). No interactive sign-in needed, so this works from a plain-HTTP DWC page.

webdav.urlHelp: e.g. https://cloud.example.com/remote.php/webdav for Nextcloud, or your Synology's WebDAV Station URL.
webdav.corsNote: If the server is on a different origin to DWC (and not a plain-HTTP server on your own network), it needs to allow this origin (CORS) or the browser will block the connection - that's between you and the server, not something this plugin controls.

encryption.heading: Credential storage & encryption
encryption.unavailable: Encryption isn't available on this connection - it needs HTTPS or localhost, the same requirement as Google Drive elsewhere on this page. Credentials are stored as plain text here (still never in a backup, never on the SD card unless you explicitly save them there).
encryption.introOff: Stored tokens/passwords are plain text in this browser by default. Turning this on encrypts them with a passphrase that's never itself stored - only you can decrypt them, and forgetting the passphrase means starting over with fresh tokens.
encryption.disableConfirmBody: Stored credentials will go back to being plain text in this browser.
encryption.sdIntro: Save the encrypted credentials to this printer's SD card so another browser or PC can load them without re-entering every token - it'll still need the same passphrase to actually use them. This stores the encrypted file on the printer itself, reachable by anything that can reach its web interface - a wider exposure than keeping credentials in just this browser.
encryption.saveToSdButton: Save to this printer's SD card
encryption.loadFromSdButton: Load from this printer's SD card
encryption.destinationsLockedNote: Destination settings are locked. Unlock above to view or edit them.
encryption.setHelp: This passphrase is never stored anywhere - only used to derive the encryption key for this session. If you forget it, stored credentials can't be recovered; you'd need to regenerate and re-enter each token.
encryption.unlockHelp: Enter the passphrase you set when you turned encryption on.
encryption.savedToSd: Saved to this printer's SD card.
encryption.loadedFromSd: Loaded from this printer's SD card - enter the passphrase to unlock.
encryption.nothingOnSd: No credentials found on this printer's SD card.

sd.not-encrypted: Turn on encryption first - this never stores plain-text credentials on the SD card.
sd.failed: Could not write to the SD card.

encryption.fileIntro: Or export the encrypted credentials as a file you move yourself (a USB stick, emailing it to yourself, etc.) - an alternative to SD-card sync when you'd rather not put the file on the printer at all. It still needs the same passphrase to unlock wherever it's imported.
encryption.exportNotEncrypted: Turn on encryption first - this never exports plain-text credentials.
encryption.importedFile: Imported - enter the passphrase to unlock.
encryption.importFileInvalid: That file doesn't look like a Flexible Layouts credential export.

tlsSetup.title: TLS / HTTPS setup
tlsSetup.openHelp: Set up HTTPS (encrypted DWC) on this printer's network interface, per RepRapFirmware 3.7's new TLS support.
tlsSetup.intro: This sets up TLS (HTTPS/FTPS/TelnetS) on the printer's own network interface - the printer serves its web UI encrypted, rather than in plain text. It needs an RRF 3.7+ board/firmware combination that supports it.
tlsSetup.noInterfaces: No network interface was found on this machine's object model.
tlsSetup.pickInterface: More than one interface can do this - pick which one to set up:
tlsSetup.noneCapable: None of this machine's network interfaces support TLS. See the reasons above.

reason.wifiFirmwareUnknown: WiFi module firmware version couldn't be read.
reason.wifiFirmwareUnparseable: WiFi module firmware version ({version}) isn't in a recognised format.
reason.wifiFirmwareTooOld: Needs WiFi module firmware 2.4.0 or later (yours reports {version}) - an ESP32-family module is also required, the ESP8266 module can't host a TLS server at all.
reason.ethernetBoardUnsupported: Ethernet TLS needs a Duet 3 MB6HC, MB6XD, or Mini 5+ - this board isn't one of those.

tlsSetup.generateIntro: Generate a private key and a self-signed certificate on your own PC. RRF only accepts an EC (P-256 or P-384) key in PEM format, with no passphrase - RSA keys and DER-encoded files are rejected.
tlsSetup.generateRequirements: OpenSSL is usually pre-installed on Linux/macOS. On Windows: install via "winget install -e --id ShiningLight.OpenSSL.Light" (if winget reports no package found, the ID has changed - run "winget search openssl" for the current one), or use Git Bash (if Git for Windows is installed) or WSL and run the same commands as Linux.
tlsSetup.generateOsNote: Run this in a terminal (Linux/macOS, Git Bash, or WSL):
tlsSetup.generateWindowsNote: This uses your machine's actual hostname/IP so the certificate matches what your browser connects to. If you access the printer by a different address too, add it to the subjectAltName as well.
tlsSetup.generatedButton: I've generated server.key and server.crt, continue
tlsSetup.uploadIntro: Select the two files you just generated. They're uploaded to 0:/sys/ - on WiFi, the next step imports them into the WiFi module's flash and the SD copies are then wiped automatically.

pemReason.notPem: This doesn't look like a PEM file (missing the ----BEGIN/END---- markers), or it's the wrong kind of file for this slot.
pemReason.encryptedKey: This private key is passphrase-protected - RRF requires a key with no passphrase. Regenerate it without one.
pemReason.wrongKeyType: This is an RSA key - RRF only accepts EC (P-256/P-384) keys. Regenerate using "openssl ecparam".

tlsSetup.enableIntro: Enable TLS on the network interface itself. This loads the uploaded key/certificate.
tlsSetup.protocolsIntro: Now choose which protocol(s) to serve over TLS:

replyReason.certMissing: RRF couldn't find server.crt on the SD card - the upload may not have completed. Try the upload step again.
replyReason.keyMissing: RRF couldn't find server.key on the SD card - the upload may not have completed. Try the upload step again.
replyReason.mismatchedPair: The key and certificate don't match, or aren't in a format RRF accepts - regenerate both files together and re-upload.
replyReason.wifiFirmwareTooOld: This WiFi module's firmware doesn't support TLS (needs 2.4.0+, and an ESP32-family module). Update the WiFi module firmware first.
replyReason.wifiNoMaterial: No TLS certificate/key found - make sure the upload step completed before enabling TLS.
replyReason.wifiRejected: The WiFi module rejected the certificate/key - regenerate both files and make sure they're an EC P-256/P-384 pair with no passphrase.

tlsSetup.persistIntro: TLS state isn't remembered across a plain M552 S1 - config.g needs its own T1 so a later reboot (or changing the SSID) doesn't silently turn TLS back off.
tlsSetup.persistNothingToDo: config.g already has everything needed - nothing to change.
tlsSetup.doneTrustNote: Because the certificate is self-signed, your browser will show a security warning the first time you connect over HTTPS - click through it, or import server.crt into your OS/browser trust store to avoid the warning. Either way the connection is encrypted; only certificate authenticity is unverified.
tlsSetup.generateInBrowserIntro: Or, since your browser supports it here (a secure HTTPS/localhost connection), generate the pair directly - no terminal needed. This only works on this one connection; the guided steps above work everywhere.
tlsSetup.reminderIntro: Show a one-click toast (never automatic renewal) when this certificate is getting close to its expiry date.
tlsSetup.reminderEnable: Remind me before this certificate expires

tlsSetup.generateWindowsToolIntro: Windows users without openssl handy: download the standalone duet-tls-cert-generator tool instead.
tlsSetup.generateWindowsToolNote: Download this file, drop it in the same folder as the unzipped tool, then run its generate-cert.bat - it generates immediately using these exact details, no typing needed.
tlsSetup.downloadArgsButton: Download details for the Windows tool
tlsSetup.enableInterfaceRestartWarning: This interface needs a brief restart to enable TLS (M552 S0, then M552 T1 S1) - the network heap is only resized on a full stop/start cycle. If you're connected to DWC through this same interface, the connection may drop for a few seconds; refresh the page if it doesn't reconnect on its own.
